rfi.title: France faces record €340bn borrowing test as government braces for 2027 budget
rfi.description: France has announced plans to borrow a record amount on the bond market next year, days before the government unveils its 2027 budget this Thursday. As the country's debt hits its highest level in 80 years and investors up their rates, ministers are under pressure to slash spending – yet surging inflation, strikes and approaching elections are setting the stage for a tussle in parliament over proposed cuts.

rfi.title: Who is Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, Morocco’s first female prime minister?
rfi.description: Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri has been named Morocco’s first female prime minister – another first for the 50-year-old lawyer, who became the first female mayor of Marrakesh 17 years ago. But who is the woman now tasked with leading Morocco’s government?

rfi.title: ‘Welcome back’: Macron and Sanchez embrace prospect of UK return to EU
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has welcomed British Prime Minister Andy Burnham's reopening of the debate over the United Kingdom's relationship with the European Union, responding to the possibility of the UK eventually rejoining the bloc with a simple message in English: “Welcome back.”

rfi.title: Exiled Burkina publisher tells RFI of repression and fear four years after coup
rfi.description: Burkina Faso on Wednesday marks four years since military strongman Captain Ibrahim Traoré took over in a coup. Comparing himself to anti-colonial icon Thomas Sankara, Traoré promised a "progressive and popular" revolution. RFI spoke to Inoussa Ouédraogo, a publishing director who now lives in exile about the country's fading human rights record.

rfi.title: Mali army and Russian fighters accused of killing dozens of civilians
rfi.description: Mali’s armed forces and Russian Wagner Group personnel committed war crimes including killings and torture of civilians during joint operations between 2023 and 2025, Amnesty International has said in a new report documenting abuses across several regions of the country.

rfi.title: US troops wrap up Iraq mission 12 years after Islamic State offensive
rfi.description: Iraq is closing a major chapter in its post-2003 history as the US-led coalition against Islamic State ends its mission – more than two decades after France opposed the invasion that toppled Saddam Hussein.

rfi.title: Eiffel Tower chief to leave after women sidelined during Hindu visit
rfi.description: Eiffel Tower director Patrick Branco Ruivo will step down at the end of the year, the tower’s operator has announced, after female staff were excluded during a visit by a Hindu religious group – an incident that triggered a strike that closed the Paris landmark for a day.

rfi.title: Rugby World Cup bosses promise big party at first 24-team tournament
rfi.description: Organisers of the 2027 Rugby World Cup on Wednesday promised a massive party during the first 24-team tournament, which starts next October in Perth, Western Australia.

rfi.title: US Supreme Court lifts limits on third-country deportations
rfi.description: The US Supreme Court on Tuesday lifted restrictions on the deportations of immigrants to countries that are not their own, while agreeing to hear the issue on its merits in December.

rfi.title: Heatwaves and wildfires drive extreme ozone pollution worldwide
rfi.description: Heatwaves, wildfires and human-caused emissions exposed a third of the world’s population to extremely high ozone pollution in 2026, with Asia worst hit and wildfire smoke crossing oceans, an EU report said on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Le Pen ally Bardella sues over antisemitism claims, alleges 'total war'
rfi.description: Jordan Bardella, a key ally of French far-right presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen, on Tuesday said allegations he made antisemitic comments in 2013 marked part of a "total war" against their National Rally party ahead of the 2027 polls. Backed by fellow party members, Bardella announced that he had filed a complaint for defamation.

rfi.title: Ghana boss Queiroz refuses to quit after poor start to 2027 AFCON qualifiers
rfi.description: Ghana head coach Carlos Queiroz on Wednesday refused to resign after his side's calamitous 4-2 defeat at home to Gambia in qualifiers for next year's Africa Cup of Nations in Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda.

rfi.title: French PM warns against student violence as public sector strike kicks off
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has warned against an escalation of the demonstrations in secondary schools, which have broken out ahead of a nationwide strike by public-sector workers. More than 100 pupils were arrested on Monday during violent clashes with police. It comes amid mounting anger over the national budget, which is due to be unveiled on Thursday.

rfi.title: French public sector workers strike over pay freeze ahead of 2027 budget
rfi.description: Teachers, healthcare workers, local government staff, tax officials and firefighters in France are on strike Tuesday to pressure the government ahead of the 2027 budget debates which could see public sector salaries frozen for a fourth straight year.

rfi.title: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger launch Tafouk TV channel to push their own narrative
rfi.description: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger are stepping up their joint media push with Tafouk TV, a new television channel aimed at challenging Western coverage and promoting the three military-led Sahel states’ own account of events.

rfi.title: French prosecutors seek 'severe' punishment for ex-minister Dati in graft case
rfi.description: France prosecutors on Monday sought two years with an electronic tag and a five-year ban on public office for ex-culture minister Rachida Dati in a trial on corruption charges linked to dealings with the Renault-Nissan group. Her lawyers have slammed the severity of the recommendations which will be announced in January next year.

rfi.title: US has 'alienated' Sudan's army in 'complex war' analyst tells RFI
rfi.description: Sudan's army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan has vowed to push on with his fight against the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces, despite a US visa snub to attend the UN General Assembly and mounting pressure for a ceasefire. RFI spoke to a Sudanese researcher about why such a step was taken and how far the stand-off could go.

rfi.title: Egypt, Senegal and Ghana face pressure to relaunch drive for 2027 AFCON

lemonde.title: Emmanuel Macron juge les propos antisémites imputés à Jordan Bardella « gravissimes et inacceptables » ; le président du RN lui répond
lemonde.description: Le chef de l’Etat a réagi, de Madrid, à l’enquête de « Mediapart » qui rapporte des propos antisémites de Jordan Bardella lorsqu’il était jeune militant du FN. « Après le 7 octobre 2023, j’ai marché dans les rues de Paris, et me suis rendu en Israël. Pas lui », a réagi le président du RN.

lemonde.title: Blocage des lycées : le ministre de l’intérieur reconnaît une « extension du mouvement » et annonce 625 interpellations
lemonde.description: Des actions ont eu lieu dans des établissements en Ile-de-France, à Lyon, Strasbourg ou Nice, le principal syndicat appelant à une poursuite de la mobilisation et à une rencontre avec le ministre de l’éducation. Ce dernier a annoncé que 119 élèves et personnels ont été blessés depuis le début du mouvement.

lemonde.title: Guerre en Ukraine : une nouvelle demande d’aide financière qui passe mal à Bruxelles
lemonde.description: Alors que l’UE commence à débourser 90 milliards d’euros pour soutenir Kiev d’ici à la fin de 2027, l’Ukraine demande déjà une rallonge de plusieurs dizaines de milliards d’euros. L’Europe cherche des solutions et pourrait devoir rouvrir le débat sur l’utilisation des avoirs russes immobilisés sur le Vieux Continent.

lemonde.title: Après la tentative de détournement d’un avion de Flydubai volant vers Tel-Aviv, des témoignages et des zones d’ombre
lemonde.description: Le vol, parti de Dubaï, a atterri mercredi en urgence en Arabie saoudite, après qu’un des pilotes a poignardé l’autre. Les autorités israéliennes n’excluent ni une attaque terroriste ni un geste suicidaire. Benyamin Nétanyahou avait mis en garde, la veille, contre des attaques éventuelles avant les élections législatives prévues pour le 27 octobre.

lemonde.title: Budget de la Sécurité sociale : les conséquences redoutées d’une absence de vote à l’Assemblée nationale
lemonde.description: Dans une Assemblée sans majorité, l’approbation du PLFSS pour 2027 semble très incertaine. En cas de blocage, la « Sécu » continuerait à verser les prestations, mais au prix d’une dégradation des comptes sociaux et d’un flou pour le secteur hospitalier et les industries pharmaceutiques.

lemonde.title: Interpellation violente à Corbeil-Essonnes : la nouvelle vidéo qui contredit la version des policiers
lemonde.description: Les images saisies par une deuxième caméra-piéton lors d’un contrôle de police qui a dégénéré, le 5 novembre 2024, dans le quartier de Montconseil, à Corbeil-Essonnes, démontrent, selon l’IGPN, « que les faits ne s[e so]nt pas déroulés tels qu’ils [o]nt été relatés par le gardien de la paix dans le procès-verbal ».

lemonde.title: Au procès de Robert Ménard pour avoir refusé de célébrer le mariage d’un homme sous OQTF, une peine d’amende requise
lemonde.description: Le maire de Béziers était poursuivi, mercredi, devant le tribunal correctionnel de Montpellier pour avoir refusé de marier un couple dont l’homme était sous le coup d’une obligation de quitter le territoire. Le procureur a requis 7 500 euros d’amende, mais pas d’inéligibilité.

lemonde.description: Atteinte d’un cancer du poumon en phase terminale, l’ancienne présentatrice avait relancé le débat sur l’aide à mourir dans son pays, ces dernières années, plaidant jusqu’au bout pour une évolution de la législation.

lemonde.description: Cette somme doit être consacrée à trois projets énergétiques dont la construction de plusieurs centrales nucléaires, d’une centrale électrique, et d’un gazoduc en Alaska.

lemonde.description: A la veille du deuxième débat de la primaire, jeudi 1ᵉʳ octobre, l’organisation de jeunesse soumet aux candidats un manifeste proposant des mesures telles que l’instauration d’un « revenu jeune ». Et espère obtenir, d’ici au premier tour de la primaire, des engagements sur des thèmes liés à la jeunesse encore sous-estimés.

france24fr.description: L'avion transportant les passagers d'un vol Flydubai qui avait été dérouté en Arabie saoudite après une altercation entre les pilotes a atterri mercredi soir à Tel-Aviv, rapporte le correspondant de France 24, Stéphane Amar. france24fr.description: Des attaques de missiles et de drones russes ont visé, dans la nuit de mardi à mercredi, le réseau énergétique ukrainien, provoquant des coupures d'électricité à Kiev. Sept personnes, dont un enfant, ont été tuées lors de ces attaques, rapportent les autorités du pays.

france24fr.title: Cancer du sein : le dépistage, pas si simple
france24fr.description: Tous les deux ans, les femmes de 50 à 74 ans sont invitées à se faire dépister gratuitement contre le cancer du sein. Mais dans la réalité, toutes n'y ont pas accès aussi facilement. Les inégalités se creusent notamment dans les endroits reculés. Pour les femmes handicapées, la réponse est loin d'être à la hauteur.

france24fr.title: "America" : Quand l'IA de Trump contredit... Trump
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a lancé un chatbot alimenté par l’Intelligence Artificielle. Le robot utilise l'IA de Gemini (Google) et de Grok (X). france24fr.title: Au Cameroun, la grève illimitée du Syndicat national des enseignants du supérieur se poursuit
france24fr.description: Au Cameroun, la rentrée universitaire prévue le 7 octobre prochain, pourrait ne pas avoir lieu. En cause, une grève illimitée déclenchée par le SYNES, le Syndicat national des enseignants du supérieur, depuis le 3 septembre 2026. spiegel.title: Tennessee: Supreme Court erlaubt Hinrichtung von Christa Pike
spiegel.description: Christa Pike wurde für den Mord an einer 19-Jährigen zum Tode verurteilt. Eine Stunde vor der Vollstreckung wurde der Termin in Tennessee gestoppt. Jetzt hat sich das oberste US-Gericht eingeschaltet.

spiegel.title: Hape Kerkeling zum AfD-Verbot: Wann, wenn nicht jetzt?
spiegel.description: Hape Kerkeling und Hans-Georg Maaßen waren dabei: Im Thüringer Landtag haben Fachleute und Prominente stundenlang über die AfD diskutiert. Der Ausgang der Debatte ist offen – und könnte wegweisend sein.

spiegel.title: Elon Musk und Pentagon: Techmilliardär soll zentrale Rolle bei »Projekt Meridian« spielen
spiegel.description: US-Verteidigungsminister Hegseth treibt ein Projekt zur Erforschung autonomer Kriegsführung voran. Dabei setzt er auf Elon Musk: Der Techmilliardär soll eine zentrale Rolle in der Initiative des Pentagon übernehmen.

spiegel.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Verlässt Portugals Nationalteam – Rücktritt offen
spiegel.description: Erst auf die Bank, dann die Abreise: Cristiano Ronaldo hat das Trainingslager der portugiesischen Nationalmannschaft verlassen. »Zu gegebener Zeit« will sich der 41-Jährige erklären.

spiegel.title: Türkei: Unabhängiges Onlineportal muss wegen angeblicher »LGBT-Propaganda« schließen
spiegel.description: Weil sie die »türkische Familienstruktur« schwächen könne, darf die Nachrichtenseite »T24« nicht länger berichten. Journalistenverbände sind entsetzt.

spiegel.title: AfD: Länder passen Beschlusspraxis aus Sorge vor Blockade an
spiegel.description: Aus Sorge vor einer Blockade durch die AfD ändern die Innenminister der Länder ihre jahrzehntelange Praxis: Künftig sollen Beschlüsse der Innenministerkonferenz auch gegen den Widerstand einzelner Länder möglich sein.

spiegel.title: AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt: Blufft Ulrich Siegmund bei der MP-Wahl?
spiegel.description: Ulrich Siegmund will im Dezember zum ersten AfD-Ministerpräsidenten Deutschlands gewählt werden. Die Rechtsextremisten behaupten, eine Mehrheit zusammenzuhaben. Stimmen muss das nicht.

spiegel.title: Ägypten: Sicherheitsapparat nimmt gesamte Redaktion von Faktencheck-Plattform »Matsada2sh« fest
spiegel.description: Bislang liegen wohl keine Angaben über den Ort der Haft oder deren Gründe vor: Ägyptische Behörden haben sechs Investigativjournalisten festgenommen – zwei davon auf offener Straße.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Mehr als 110 Verletzte bei Schulprotesten – 625 Festnahmen
spiegel.description: Die Lage an französischen Schulen eskaliert weiter: Nach Angaben der Regierung wurden über 600 Menschen festgenommen. Einige Personen haben Jugendliche offenbar gezielt zu Gewalt angestiftet.

spiegel.title: Wahlkampfhilfe für Donald Trump: USA wollen Europas Diesel-Vorräte freipressen
spiegel.description: Donald Trump steht vor den Zwischenwahlen mit dem Rücken zur Wand. Nun versucht er offenbar, die Europäer zur Freigabe ihrer strategischen Dieselreserven zu zwingen – um die Preise in den USA zu drücken.

spiegel.title: Irak: USA beenden Anti-IS-Militäreinsatz nach mehr als einem Jahrzehnt
spiegel.description: Die letzten US-Soldaten haben den Irak verlassen. Donald Trump prahlt zum Abschied von einem Sieg über die Terrormiliz »IS« und bezeichnet den Einsatz im Zweistromland als »Sumpf«.

spiegel.title: Marokko: König Mohammed VI. ernennt Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri zur erste Premierministerin
spiegel.description: Mohammed VI. macht weiter seine eigene Politik. Der marokkanische Monarch unterhält beste Beziehungen zu Israel und hat nun auch die erste Frau als Ministerpräsidentin eingesetzt – eine erfahrene Politikerin.

spiegel.title: Nato: Militärbündnis erhält Westfälischen Friedenspreis in Münster
spiegel.description: Das Verteidigungsbündnis wird in Münster für seinen Beitrag zur europäischen Friedensordnung ausgezeichnet. Bundeskanzler Merz hält die Laudatio, Nato-Generalsekretär Rutte nimmt den Preis entgegen.

spiegel.title: Israel-Gaza-Krieg: Kino-Start der umstrittenen Gaza-Doku »Naza«
spiegel.description: Im Dokumentarfilm »Naza« enthüllen israelische Soldaten die brutale Kriegsführung in Gaza. Israels Regierung wirft den Machern Landesverrat vor. Nun kommt der Film in die Kinos. Der SPIEGEL hat ihn gesehen.

spiegel.title: Bündnis Sahra Wagenknecht BSW: Partei streicht Namen der Gründerin
spiegel.description: Das Bündnis Sahra Wagenknecht streicht den Namen seiner Gründerin aus dem Parteinamen. Die Partei heißt ab dem 1. Oktober offiziell anders. Das Kürzel bleibt aber bestehen.

spiegel.title: Israel: Passagiere aus Flydubai-Maschine in Tel Aviv gelandet
spiegel.description: Ein Ersatzflug brachte sie an ihr Ziel: Die Israelis an Bord von Flug FZ1073 können vorerst aufatmen. Angehörige begrüßten sie in Tel Aviv mit Blumen und Luftballons.

spiegel.title: Bundestag: Linke-Abgeordnete Ferat Koçak gibt Sitz im Innenausschuss ganz auf
spiegel.description: In einer Stellungnahme räumte er einen »Fehler« ein: Der Bundestagsabgeordnete Ferat Koçak gibt nach Kritik an zu viel Nähe zu mutmaßlichen Angehörigen krimineller Clans seinen Sitz im Innenausschuss ganz auf.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: Diese KI-Bosse waren ihm beim »Super Intelligence Luncheon« besonders nah
spiegel.description: Das Ergebnis der jüngsten KI-Runde in Washington ist mau. Doch US-Präsident Trump setzt auf Symbolik und starke Bilder. Das Schaulaufen der Tech-Elite in der Grafikanalyse.

observador.title: Como o "caso-não caso" se tornou o fim de Ronaldo na Seleção
observador.description: Proença antecipou viagem por saber que Ronaldo podia deixar estágio. Não foi aí, foi 24 horas depois. Pelo meio, houve a conferência de Jesus. Antes, vários capítulos. A partir de agora, ninguém sabe.

observador.title: USF: médico de família para todos até 2029
observador.description: Aposentações a cair e internos em formação em número suficiente. A USF-AN diz que a estatística joga a favor — mas avisa que não basta abrir vagas.

observador.title: CESA alerta para défice açoriano de 5% do PIB
observador.description: O Conselho Económico e Social dos Açores analisou as contas de 2025 e deixa avisos sobre o fim do PRR, dívida pública e atrasos no pagamento a fornecedores.

observador.title: Violação. Cornell avança com investigação independente
observador.description: Jovem denunciou que em 2024 foi embriagada, drogada e violada em grupo na casa de uma fraternidade ligada a Cornell. A universidade prepara revisão externa sobre a forma como o caso foi tratado.

observador.title: 40% dos jovens com sintomas depressivos nas escolas
observador.description: Programa "Mais Contigo" abrangeu 18.651 alunos no último ano letivo. Mais de 2.100 adolescentes foram identificados em risco de comportamento suicidário.

observador.title: 00h. Montenegro sublinha "sinal importante" dado pelo PS
observador.description: Montenegro elogia o sinal dado pelo PS em relação à eventual viabilização do OE para 2027. Ainda, Cristiano Ronaldo já está a caminho de Madrid.

observador.title: Parque Papa Francisco: concerto cancelado após problemas
observador.description: A decisão surge depois de incidentes graves no último evento, com milhares de pessoas acumuladas junto à Linha do Norte — já o concerto de David Guetta, em agosto, tinha gerado situação semelhante.

observador.title: Festival da Natureza tem investimento de 221 mil euros
observador.description: Yoga, arte circense, Festival da Baleia e Echoo Madeira Nature Fest são algumas das novidades. Ocupação hoteleira ronda os 91%, semelhante à do ano anterior.

observador.description: A Doutrina da Guerra nas Crónicas Medievais Portuguesas: do Mito à Legitimação do Estado

observador.title: Brasil denuncia tentativas de interferência russa e dos EUA
observador.description: Ações dos Estados Unidos podem ir "desde a instrumentalização do sistema judicial até uma ingerência abertamente reconhecida", enquanto não são conhecidas as tentativas por parte de Moscovo.

observador.title: Nissan Pixo, o citadino que nasce do Twingo e do novo Spring
observador.description: A Nissan apresentou o novo Pixo, um modelo citadino e eléctrico que promete ser dos mais eficientes e acessíveis do mercado. Recorre à base do Twingo E-Tech e será fabricado pela Renault na Eslovénia.

observador.title: Santa Maria da Feira mais do que duplica apoio aos bombeiros
observador.description: Cada uma das três corporações passa a receber 254.000 euros por ano. Os protocolos foram assinados esta quarta-feira e têm efeitos retroativos a janeiro de 2026.

observador.title: Nova associação de vítimas pede à CEP que aceite auditoria
observador.description: A associação "Dar Voz ao Silêncio" entrega na quinta-feira um dossiê à Conferência Episcopal e responsabiliza também o Estado pelos abusos cometidos.

observador.title: "Perguntem ao Queiroz" e o Qatar: as outras polémicas de CR7
observador.description: Cristiano Ronaldo nunca tinha chegado ao ponto de abandonar o estágio da Seleção, mas já tinha protagonizado várias polémicas — entre a boca a Fernando Santos, o tiro a Queiroz e a braçadeira no chão.

observador.title: "Bomba em Portugal": imprensa internacional sobre Ronaldo
observador.description: De Espanha ao Reino Unido, jornais internacionais descrevem uma "enorme crise" em Portugal, as palavras do selecionador que "incendiaram tudo" e o fim "Iminente" da carreira de Ronaldo.

observador.title: Oposição questiona câmara sobre queixas de ruído na Estrela
observador.description: PS, PCP e BE questionaram o executivo de Moedas sobre as queixas dos moradores. A vereadora Joana Baptista admite ilegalidade urbanística, mas garante que os eventos têm licença de ruído.

observador.title: Marcha contra imigração ilegal nas ruas de Durban
observador.description: Nos protestos, as pessoas exigiam mais segurança e vigilância contra a violência de género. Os manifestantes culpam os migrantes pelo aumento da criminalidade e pelos problemas económicos.

nyt.title: Trump’s Voluntary A.I. Policing Echoes What Biden Did. But Is It Enough Today?
nyt.description: President Trump’s plan to let A.I. companies police themselves comes amid mounting examples that they are failing to put safeguards on the technology.

nyt.title: Congress Set to Leave Washington for the Midterms With No A.I. Progress
nyt.description: Senate Democrats blocked a measure that would encourage, but not require, states to protect consumers from power rate hikes tied to data center growth, and had no limits on A.I. use or deployment.

nyt.title: OpenAI’s Greg Brockman Backs Out of Second $25 Million Donation to A.I. Super PAC
nyt.description: Greg Brockman, OpenAI’s president and co-founder, said internally that the super PAC, Leading the Future, had become a “distraction” for the A.I. company.

nyt.title: Who Attended Trump’s AI Luncheon, and Who Sat Where
nyt.description: A seating chart of the meeting illustrated growing divisions within the artificial intelligence industry and how it is viewed by the White House.

nyt.title: Plane to Israel Narrowly Averts Disaster
nyt.description: Also, a Kelvin wave is heading to California. Here’s the latest at the end of Wednesday.

nyt.title: A Bloody Attack on a FlyDubai Plane Headed to Israel, and a Terrifying Plunge
nyt.description: “I don’t deserve to die like this,” said one passenger on Flight 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The motive of the cockpit stabbing remains unknown, officials said.

nyt.title: Panic and Heroics on FlyDubai Flight: ‘We Felt That This Was It’
nyt.description: A routine flight turned terrifying when a violent altercation broke out inside the cockpit and the aircraft dropped 17,000 feet in two minutes. Passengers subdued a knife-wielding attacker.

nyt.title: Supreme Court Allows Execution of Christa Pike, Tennessee’s Lone Woman on Death Row
nyt.description: Christa Pike tortured and murdered a classmate in 1995. She had been set to die on Wednesday, the first woman executed in the state in 200 years, until a lower court paused the execution.

nyt.title: In Speech, Hegseth Targets Diversity, Transgender People, Reporters and Iran
nyt.description: In his “State of the Force” address, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth focused on the culture war and accused reporters of “treason” over Iran war coverage.

nyt.title: Hegseth Talks Tough as Republican Doubts About His Leadership Grow
nyt.description: Pete Hegseth has held onto his job by projecting a tough guy image, but his relationship with Republican lawmakers has never been worse.

nyt.title: Cornell Students Question Greek Life Culture After Sexual Assault Claim
nyt.description: With their university under fire in the wake of a sexual assault lawsuit, students are having difficult conversations about Greek life, campus rituals and the possibility for lasting changes.

nyt.title: What New York’s Rape Laws Mean for the Cornell Case
nyt.description: State law makes it harder to prosecute when victims drank willingly. The prosecutor in the Cornell case said that kept him from charging students accused of sexual assault.

nyt.title: Chi Phi Says It Acted Quickly in 2024 to Expel Cornell Members Named in Sexual Assault Lawsuit
nyt.description: The national organization of the Chi Phi fraternity at the center of a Cornell University sexual assault lawsuit explained publicly for the first time how it handled the episode.

nyt.title: Democrats Block Stock-Trading Bill, Denying the G.O.P. a Pre-Midterm Win
nyt.description: A Republican measure to limit, but not bar, congressional stock trading faltered in the Senate as Democrats thwarted a G.O.P. bid to show progress on an issue that has rankled voters.

nyt.title: Becerra and Hilton to Face Off in Televised California Governor Debate
nyt.description: Xavier Becerra, a Democrat who served in the Biden administration, will debate Steve Hilton, a Republican former talk show host, in what’s likely to be their only face-off before the election.

nyt.title: Andrea Shaw Says Vaccines Killed Her Twins. Authorities Say She Suffocated Them.
nyt.description: In a small Idaho town, a young mother is accused of killing her young twins. She blames the childhood vaccines they received.

nyt.title: Fed’s Watchdog Finds No Misconduct or Illegal Activity in Costly Renovations
nyt.description: A new report by the Federal Reserve’s independent inspector general concluded that a nearly $2.5 billion construction project was poorly managed but made no referrals to the U.S. attorney general.

nyt.title: Justice Dept. Tries to Rebuke Federal Judges for Speaking to The Times
nyt.description: Judge Patrick J. Schiltz had warned that the administration’s actions “created a grave threat to the rule of law.” The attorney general accused him of “obvious bias.”

npr.title: Swiss glaciers suffer another year of record ice loss
npr.description: Switzerland's glaciers are disappearing at a record pace. More than 5% of their ice has vanished this year alone — threatening water supplies, ecosystems and communities across Europe.

npr.title: Greetings from Syria, where time seems to melt as a glassmaker braves scorching temps
npr.description: As a Syrian glassmaker created his wares in Damascus, watching his craft reminded this reporter to slow down and enjoy the moment.

npr.title: How Ukrainians are coping with new, more deadly Russian attacks
npr.description: Zanny Minton Beddoes, The Economist's editor in chief, just visited Ukraine. She says, despite all its drone weaponry, Kyiv is under extraordinary bombardment, as Russia tries to make it unlivable.

npr.title: On flight to Israel, pilot is stabbed, plane plunges before passengers tackle attacker
npr.description: As the plane went into a spin and began to plunge, passengers and crew members got into the cockpit, subdued the pilot and diverted the flight to land in Saudi Arabia, Israel's leader says.

npr.title: U.S. forces exit Iraq amid Iran war. And, SCOTUS revives Trump deportation policy
npr.description: The U.S. has withdrawn its final troops from Iraq, leaving its defense future uncertain. And, the Supreme Court has sided for now with the Trump administration on third-country deportations.

npr.title: The U.S. military withdraws from Iraq over 2 decades after its invasion
npr.description: 23 years after the United States military invaded Iraq, sparking an insurgency and a civil war, the U.S. has withdrawn its forces, as the country still tries to combat Iranian influence.

npr.title: Retired general who led troops in Iraq warns U.S. exit may give Iran, ISIS an opening
npr.description: Retired Lt. Gen. H.R. McMaster, who commanded U.S. troops in Iraq, says the withdrawal could strengthen Iran and leave Iraq more vulnerable to ISIS.

npr.title: An 87-year-old woman whose eviction sparked protests in Spain is returning home
npr.description: María del Carmen Abascal's case has drawn tens of thousands of people to the streets in recent days and led the Spanish government to present measures to address the country's housing crisis.

npr.title: Potential Taiwan tension sparked 'last minute' change in Trump-Xi National Archives visit
npr.description: The sudden change was precipitated because of Chinese displeasure over one document that the U.S. had planned to show.

npr.title: Trump weakens fuel efficiency standards. And, Cornell fraternity rape case reopened
npr.description: The Trump administration has weakened fuel efficiency standards for new cars. And, prosecutors have reopened a Cornell University fraternity rape case.

elpais.description: Los pasajeros y un miembro de la tripulación redujeron al agresor. El ministro israelí de Defensa denuncia un intento de “atentado yihadista” que pretendía estrellar el aparato, procedente de Dubái

elpais.title: El intento de secuestro de aviones vinculados a Israel, una amenaza que viene de los años sesenta
elpais.description: Las milicias palestinas multiplicaron las tentativas hace medio siglo para exigir liberaciones de presos

elpais.title: Rusia amenaza con usar armas nucleares contra los países de la OTAN en plena escalada de tensión en el Báltico
elpais.description: Moscú ha advertido a la Alianza en una nota diplomática de que no debe intentar aislar Kaliningrado. La Alianza acusa a Moscú de usar una “retórica nuclear irresponsable”

elpais.title: La Aemet alerta de “peligro elevado” por un frente y una dana que afectarán de jueves a lunes al tercio oriental
elpais.description: Se trata de chubascos muy fuertes y persistentes que “pueden dar lugar a inundaciones locales súbitas y repentinas” en zonas bajas, arroyos y ramblas

elpais.title: El casero tendrá que indemnizar con 12 mensualidades al inquilino si decide no renovar el alquiler
elpais.description: El Ejecutivo retrasa un día la publicación en el BOE del segundo decreto de vivienda, que incluye la prórroga indefinida de los contratos y tendrá que votarse en el Congreso

elpais.title: ¿Cómo afectan los decretos de vivienda a los acampados en Sol?
elpais.description: Los manifestantes debaten sobre las medidas aprobadas en el Consejo de Ministros

elpais.title: Un dilema en Sol: cuándo parar
elpais.description: Los jóvenes acampados por la vivienda en Madrid dudan si levantar las tiendas el fin de semana, en medio de una sensación de euforia, o arriesgarse a extender la protesta de manera indefinida

elpais.title: Una secuencia de vídeo para mostrar el interior del ‘campamento de las mil tiendas’ de la Puerta del Sol
elpais.description: Una cámara de EL PAÍS camina por las instalaciones montadas en la plaza, que ha ido creciendo a medida que se han incorporado más jóvenes a la protesta

Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

undark.title: Interview: What Does the ‘I’ in AI Really Mean?
undark.description: Is it possible that AI is — or might one day become — truly intelligent? Undark posed the question to five experts in linguistics, computer science, cognitive science, and psychology. They offered very different answers, though they agreed that the term “intelligence” is vague and poorly suited to the debate.

undark.title: Book Excerpt: Why the Brain Isn’t the Self
undark.description: The brain isn’t the self — consciousness is intimately linked with the human body. And if consciousness is the body’s way of knowing itself, then it is the living form in its entirety that should be taken as selfhood proper, with the brain as an especially feverish region.

public-dom.title: Philip Sidney and the Extreme (Dis)graces of the Parenthesis
public-dom.description: Erasmus called them “little moons” and George Puttenham praised them as “figures of tolerable disorder” (if used not too often “nor too thick”). For Philip Sidney, they were simply indispensable. Florence Hazrat introduces us to the uncontested early modern king of brackets and to his romance Arcadia, which abruptly ends, like its author’s life, hanging on a parenthesis.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Vanity Summit With Xi
proj-syn.description: While expectations for the summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping were low, it was disappointing to watch them prioritize pageantry over substance. Trump’s cringe-worthy declarations of heartfelt admiration for Xi reflect his twisted sense that the trappings of power are power itself.

proj-syn.title: Human Rights and Populist Wrongs
proj-syn.description: For the first time, all the UK’s political parties on the right favor withdrawing from the European Convention on Human Rights. But the story of the Hillsborough Law shows how human-rights laws, not least the ECHR, help ordinary people hold the state accountable for its costliest failings.

proj-syn.title: Is Another Eurozone Debt Crisis Looming?
proj-syn.description: At a time when the cost of servicing sovereign debt is rising globally, France stands out as an especially fragile case. Its public debt-to-GDP ratio is edging up toward that of Greece on the eve of its sovereign-debt crisis, and the French political system seems unable to do anything about it.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Reverse the Renminbi’s Rise?
proj-syn.description: In China, AI-driven productivity gains will most likely be in non-tradable services, which could push down relative prices and put downward pressure on the renminbi’s real exchange rate. To ensure that this does not also mean lower income and weaker demand, policymakers should ensure that the productivity dividend is broadly shared.

proj-syn.title: The Price of You
proj-syn.description: As more people shop online, firms are increasingly setting individualized prices based on personal data, including purchase history, location, demographics, behavior, and biometric data. AI threatens to turbocharge such surveillance pricing, further widening the gap between privacy expectations and reality.

proj-syn.title: Investing in Brain Health
proj-syn.description: Just as AI agents are mastering complex cognitive tasks, our own ability to perform the same tasks is eroding. Whether AI vindicates its boosters or fizzles out like the Metaverse craze of 2022, we will not fare well without a civilization-wide effort to rebuild the cognitive skills that make technological progress possible.

proj-syn.title: Europe Still Needs Molecules
proj-syn.description: Not even the most effective European electrification strategy will eliminate the need for the molecules that fossil fuels provide. Given this, Europe must diversify its oil and gas supplies, maintain its refining capacity, and lock in decarbonization by building a hydrogen-energy industry at scale.

proj-syn.title: Energy Security in an Age of Disruption
proj-syn.description: While there is no single prescription for energy security, strengthening “response capacity,” such as by establishing stockpiles, substituting sources, and diversifying suppliers, is essential. The point is not to eliminate vulnerabilities altogether, but to ensure that there are options when disruption arrives.

proj-syn.title: Africa’s Common Currency-in-Waiting
proj-syn.description: While the phased approach of the Economic Community of West African States to implementing a long-delayed single currency will maintain momentum without compromising macroeconomic discipline, the bloc still lacks a robust mechanism to address asymmetric shocks. That is why fiscal integration must come first.

proj-syn.title: Learning to Reconcile
proj-syn.description: Political discourse in many Western countries has broken down, making it difficult for people with different viewpoints to live amicably with one another. The Reconciliation League, an international initiative by 13 universities and colleges, aims to train a generation of leaders who can change that.

proj-syn.title: Sheinbaum Is Just Another Trump Appeaser
proj-syn.description: After two years in office, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum continues to be widely praised, both in Mexico and abroad, for her handling of US President Donald Trump. But Sheinbaum has skillfully—and cynically—disguised the extent to which she has deferred to Trump on almost every issue.

proj-syn.title: Distorted Intelligence at the AI Frontier
proj-syn.description: The real problem for the frontier AI labs is not that their models are too powerful and already “misaligned” with the goals their creators set for them. Rather, it is that the models are being trained in ways that may be leading to a type of intelligence that will become less predictable.

proj-syn.title: Good Growth Requires the Right Public Finance
proj-syn.description: Although the Labour Party has done more to strengthen the United Kingdom's public-finance ecosystem in the past two years than any government in a generation, it must not stop there. If public investment is to meet its full potential, it must be reorganized to operate at scale on the public's behalf.

proj-syn.title: An EU–Canada Partnership Against Coercion
proj-syn.description: By proposing that the European Union and Canada begin work toward an association agreement, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has taken a critical first step toward establishing Europe as a hub for the world’s democratic middle powers. Such an arrange

proj-syn.title: The Opposing Forces Reshaping Global Finance
proj-syn.description: The financial industry is being pulled between two powerful forces: bottom-up financial technology is enabling seamless integration, while top-down geoeconomic statecraft is promoting fragmentation. So much for the conventional wisdom that finance will simply become smoother, cheaper, and more globalized over time.

proj-syn.title: The Dismally Obedient Science
proj-syn.description: While empirical inquiry has its place in economics, the pursuit of causality must not be allowed to displace the pursuit of explanation. Beyond identifying causal effects within existing arrangements, economists must investigate how those arrangements are produced, reproduced, and contested.

proj-syn.title: Oligarchy Is a Symptom, Not a Cause
proj-syn.description: The deepening political dysfunction plaguing the US can be traced not to wealth inequality, as some argue, but to the fact that different groups of voters believe different facts. A political strategy that takes this into account might eventually lead to wealth redistribution, but it must begin with improved critical-thinking skills.

proj-syn.title: The Immigrants Leading the Anti-Immigrant Far Right
proj-syn.description: Right-wing populists have turned hypocrisy into a successful electoral strategy. But those voting for nativism in Europe and the United States should be careful what they wish for: They may end up expelling their own family members, if not their own political leaders.
